After 
Coding 
Round 
and 
Video
Interview, 15 students were selected for
the CFG (Code for Good Hackathon)

Before Hackathon:
=> Before the hackathon, a list came out with about seven people
in each group, totaling around 550 individuals from different
states, some from NIT or IIT, and others from local colleges. Then,
we connected through LinkedIn and Slack. The most important
platforms were Slack and Zoom, and there was one more thing (I
can't recall, but it was for code submission; don't worry, they
would explain how to download it before the hackathon started).
=> After the initial meeting, we created WhatsApp groups to get to
know each other and find out about everyone's tech stack
preferences, such as who does frontend or backend, API, or
database work.
=> Later, we had a Zoom meeting where they explained the
submission process and answered any doubts we had. We also
received a list of mentors. Basically, we had three mentors, with
only two conducting interviews, while the third observed the
teams. We got to know the mentors, who were all very friendly.
=> After that, the problem statements were released. There were
four in total, but we could only choose three. We discussed this
among ourselves and with the mentors via WhatsApp and Zoom.
The submission process for the problem statements was first in,
first out (FIFO), so be ready to submit quickly, or you might end up
with the second or third problem statement.
Code for Good Hackathon
This is the final step for SEP Selection Process
Interview were conducted Online and duration is 24
hours.

During Hackathon:
=>During the hackathon, I served as a full-stack developer. Since my team
lacked expertise in backend development, I and one other member took on
the backend tasks while the rest focused on frontend work. We were deeply
engaged in solving problems and interacting with mentors, which was crucial
for our progress. We had extensive discussions about the backend challenges
we encountered and sought guidance from mentors.
There were two rounds of interviews, conducted one-on-one for each team
member. The first round took place around 12:30 at night. The questions asked
were:
What tech stack have you learned?
1.
Can you describe a project you've worked on, and about hackathons
you've participated in?
2.
Are you enjoying this hackathon?
3.
Have you completed your tasks so far? (Even if you haven't completed
them, don't worry, they won't be disappointed)
4.
What subjects were you taught in college?
5.
Only two questions were related to subjects:
Explain joins and types of joins? (From DBMS)
1.
Tell me about data structures and provide a real-life example (From DSA)
2.
After the interviews, I continued working on the backend tasks, such as
creating APIs and databases. All team members worked smoothly, although it
took time to complete our tasks.
Later, a second interview was conducted by another mentor around 5:30 in
the morning. Similar questions were asked (as in the first round (1,2,3)), along
with inquiries about any doubts we had and details about our college life and
extracurricular activities. There were no questions about subjects in this
round.
We had three tasks to complete: creating a website, submitting our code on
GitHub, and preparing a presentation and screen recording. We divided our
work accordingly, and the submission deadline was 10 a.m.

After Hackathon:
=>Somehow, we managed to complete both the backend and frontend tasks,
although not fully. We submitted our work and then took a break. Later, it was
announced that presentations would begin at 11 a.m. We did our best and
delivered our presentation, and the organizers were pleased with our solution.
Following the presentations, the results were announced, and to our delight,
we made it to the final round. We were incredibly excited about this. 
We gave our final presentation in the final round, but unfortunately, We didn't
win the hackathon.
=> Despite not winning, we were still thrilled because we had enjoyed the
hackathon immensely, and the mentors were excellent. It was a really positive
experience getting to know others, learning about their tech stacks, and
gaining new insights.
Tips:
Interaction with mentors and communication is the most important
thing.
1.
Even if you have only done frontend work, don't be afraid. It's not about
the tech stack you used; it's about the solution you provide.
2.
Focus on important subjects like DBMS and OS for interviews.
3.
Regularly practice DSA questions (450Sheet or Striver Sheet) and make
sure to attend hackathons (I used Coding Ninjas and LeetCode Platform).
4.
Forget to mention that a Git Workshop was also conducted before the
hackathon, where you learned about Git and GitHub.
5.
Even if you didn't win, don't be disappointed because it's not about
winning; it's about how well you participate in the hackathon. 
6.
Be confident, relaxed, and don't be shy. Also, avoid arguing with mentors.
7.
Intership Offer: 
After 1 month, internship result were announced, 6 out of 10 received
internship offers (from college), and all 6 accepted the offer since the results
were announced
From my Hackathon Team , 4 out of 7 received the offers.
